title: Render an anchor chip on anchored comment threads
description:
Extend the single renderer renderThread in src/thread.js so a thread object carrying an anchor renders a chip element naming that anchor inside the thread markup. Threads with no anchor must render byte-identically to today's output (`
${body}
`). The characterisation (golden) tests that pin today's anchor-less markup ride along in THIS ticket as supporting tests — they are not a separate ticket; the new anchored-chip tests supply the red. Do not add a second renderer. Creating or editing anchors is out of scope. Chip visual styling is judged by the captain at Verify. Tests live in tests/ and run with `node --test tests`.

acceptanceCriteria.text: renderThread({ body, anchor }) with a non-empty anchor returns markup containing a chip element (e.g. class "anchor-chip") inside the thread div whose text content is the anchor's name
acceptanceCriteria.serves: An anchored thread renders a chip naming its anchor

acceptanceCriteria.text:
renderThread({ body }) with no anchor (anchor absent, undefined, null or empty string) returns exactly `
` + body + `
`, byte-for-byte equal to the pre-change output
acceptanceCriteria.serves: An anchor-less thread renders byte-identically to today

acceptanceCriteria.text: Golden tests in tests/ assert strict string equality of renderThread output for several anchor-less inputs (plain body, empty body, body containing HTML-special characters) against literal expected strings captured from today's renderer, and run under `node --test tests`
acceptanceCriteria.serves: The current anchor-less output is protected by tests so a later change cannot silently alter it

acceptanceCriteria: The existing test in tests/thread.test.js continues to pass
seamsNote: renderThread is a pure function from a thread object to a string; this ticket writes no state that another code path reads back.
entrypointsNote: this ticket adds no CLI command and no CI workflow; tests run via the existing `node --test tests` command.
rationale: The mission is one behaviour change in one renderer. The validated plan's golden tests pin existing anchor-less output, so on their own they would pass on the parent commit and could not be proved by flip-flop; they are folded into the ticket that changes renderThread, where the new anchored-chip tests provide the red and the goldens guard the anchor-less branch while it is edited.
